nextStoryContext: US-R6-003 fixed the exact gap the reviewer found: test/integration/stop-defaultlistprocesses-real.test.ts's US-R4-001 test hand-rolled the fd-open/spawn/stdio-redirect shape in its own body (buildSidecarRespawnArgv + a manual openSync + Bun.spawn(...,{stdio:['ignore',logFd,logFd]})) instead of calling the production makeSpawnSidecarFn closure (src/commands/sidecar-liveness-watch.ts), which was not even exported. Reverting the production fix left the old test green -- not falsifiable. Fix: exported `makeSpawnSidecarFn(cwd, argvOverride?)`, the SAME closure runSidecarLivenessWatch wires by default via `options.spawnSidecarFn ?? makeSpawnSidecarFn(cwd)` -- no change to that call site or to any existing behavior (argvOverride defaults to the real buildSidecarRespawnArgv(process.execPath, process.argv[1]) self-invoke when omitted). The `argvOverride` parameter is a narrow, deliberate DI seam: it exists ONLY because under `bun test`, process.argv[1] is the test file's own path, so calling the real production default from inside a test would self-invoke and respawn the entire test suite as a child process. The rewritten test now calls the real exported makeSpawnSidecarFn(projectCwd, respawnArgv)() directly, with respawnArgv still built via the real buildSidecarRespawnArgv but pointed at a lightweight idle marker script instead of the test file itself -- the fd open/redirect/close logic under test is now byte-for-byte the shipped production code, only the self-invoke TARGET is swapped for test-safety. SidecarLivenessWatchProcessHandle only exposes {pid, kill} (no .exited promise), so the post-SIGTERM liveness assertion switched from `await proc.exited` to a signal-0 waitForCondition poll -- same assertion strength, different mechanism, no test.helpers change needed. Falsifiability verified empirically (not just by inspection), per the project's tautological-oracle sweep convention: temporarily reverted the stdio line in makeSpawnSidecarFn back to ['ignore','ignore','ignore'] (the pre-US-R4-001 state), re-ran the rewritten test, confirmed it failed with a real waitForCondition timeout (the respawned process was genuinely invisible to defaultListProcesses's fallback scan), then restored the fix and confirmed green again -- this is the proof the old test never had. Full quality spine green: typecheck 0 errors, bun test 5935 pass/0 fail (unchanged count -- no new test cases added, the existing US-R4-001 test was rewritten in place, not duplicated), bun run check:all all-green (lint/file-size/debt-markers/version-skips/coverage/dead-code/dup/ci-parity/agents-md/test-sleeps/skip-ratchet), no vendor/templates touched so embed-vendor gates n/a, no file-size budget edit needed. Appended one patterns.md bullet under the sidecar/CAM-482 thread: the general lesson that any production closure self-invoking via buildSelfSpawnArgv/resolveSelfInvokeArgv needs the same argv-override DI seam if a future story wants to test it directly, since process.argv[1] under bun test always resolves to the test file itself. This story exhausts the currently known US-R6-* review findings for CAM-482 (US-R6-001 internal-contracts pin, US-R6-002 fd leak, US-R6-003 test falsifiability); next dispatch is whatever the supervisor's review cycle surfaces after this round.
